To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
compressive strain and tensile strains both increased the thicknesses of the IMC layers.
compressive strain and tensile strains both increased the thickness and separation of the Cu–Sn IMCs.
compressive strain enhances Cu–Sn IMC growth, while tensile strain does not have as strong an effect on the growth of Cu 3 Sn and Cu 6 Sn 4 IMC layers.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation of IMC on the Cu–Sn interconnects under the influence of strain.
the effects of in-plane strain on the growth of IMCs at the Cu/Sn interface.
the effects of substrate stress on the growth and morphology of inter-metallic compounds in a solder joint.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
compressive strain enhances IMC formation, whereas tensile strain has a detrimental effect on the growth of the IMC.
compressive strain increases the IMC layer thickness, and tensile strain has the opposite effect, but the effect of tensile strain is less significant.
the growth rate of the IMCs is dependent on the applied strain, the aging time and the temperature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the strain induced in the silicon substrate during the bending process has a significant influence on the IMC growth.
strain enhanced out-distribution of Cu atoms towards the Sn layer is responsible for the increased thickness of the IMCs, which is consistent with the findings of previous research.
the growth of inter-metallics can be controlled by the introduction of in-plane strain.
The main takeaway from our work is that
compressive strain can be used to accelerate the formation of Cu–Sn IMC in solder joints.
the growth of IMCs is highly dependent on the strain in the underlying substrate.
the strain induced in a substrate can be used to control the growth of interfacial IMCs.
